lab: Design and Analysis of Algorithms Virtual Lab
lab_display_name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms Virtual Lab
introduction:
The Design and Analysis of Algorithms (DAA) Virtual Lab is a dynamic platform that enables users to explore the fundamental concepts and practical applications of algorithms in Computer Science. Algorithms form the backbone of efficient problem-solving and are essential for developing optimized software solutions across a wide range of domains, including data processing, artificial intelligence, networking, and system design. Understanding how algorithms are designed, analyzed, and optimized is essential for improving performance, reducing computational complexity, and ensuring scalability in software systems.
In this virtual laboratory, students will explore the principles of algorithm design and analysis, focusing on developing efficient solutions to complex computational problems.

experiments.name: Divide and Conquer Strategies I: Sorting
Divide and Conquer Strategies II: Closest Pair of Points
Greedy Algorithms I: Coin Change Problem
Dynamic Programming I: Longest Common Subsequence (LCS)
Dynamic Programming II: Rod Cutting Problem

objective:
The objectives of the Design and Analysis of Algorithms Virtual Lab are:
  • To provide a practical understanding of the importance of efficient analysis and design of algorithms from the perspectives of both time and space complexity
  • To develop familiarity with major algorithms and underlying data structures
  • To apply algorithm design strategies such as divide-and-conquer paradigm, dynamic programming, greedy algorithms, backtracking and heuristics as appropriate
  • To gain the ability to design and implement efficient algorithms in common engineering design situations
